GANNA: ‘I Want Ukrainian Folk Music to Be Heard for Its Beauty, Not Because of War’ — For more than a decade, Berlin-based Ukrainian artist GANNA has explored and reimagined traditional Ukrainian songs through jazz, electronics and improvisation. Ahead of her performance at the Vyrii Festival, she speaks to Kyiv Post about preserving living traditions, Europe’s growing interest in Ukrainian culture, and why folk music continues to shape her artistic mission.

Turkey Restricts Black Sea Shipping, Urges Moratorium — Turkey has restricted the movement of commercial vessels heading to the Black Sea via the Dardanelles, targeting routes to the Russian port of Novorossiysk and potentially Ukrainian ports. The move follows a surge in violence in the region, which recently injured several Turkish crew members. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has called on both Kyiv and Moscow to establish a moratorium on targeting commercial ships.

Patriot Production in Ukraine to Take Years, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that setting up domestic production of Patriot air defense systems will take between 12 months and several years due to US bureaucratic delays. Speaking on national television, Zelensky claimed that the US president and key institutions have already made the political decision to transfer the necessary licenses to Kyiv.

Ukraine Buys 70 ATACMS Missiles From Turkey — The US State Department has notified Congress of a proposed transfer of US-made weapons from Turkey to Ukraine. Published in the Congressional Record on Aug. 6, the massive package includes 70 M39 ATACMS ballistic missiles, 12 M270 MLRS launchers, and thousands of cluster munitions. The transfer, handled by Turkish, Bulgarian, and US logistics firms, is pending congressional review.

Dragon Capital, the KSE Institute and the National Bank of Ukraine presented 2026 GDP forecasts ranging from 1% to 1.8% at the same event.

Kyiv’s Saint Sophia Cathedral Launches Official English Audio Guide — Kyiv’s iconic Saint Sophia Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage site, has launched a new English-language audio guide. The voice of the guide is Andy Hunder, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine, who invites international visitors to explore the cathedral’s thousand-year history, mosaics, frescoes and architecture.

Kim Jong Un Reaps $22 Billion Windfall from Russian Alliance — North Korea amassed up to $22 billion in foreign revenue between 2022 and 2025, primarily by supplying arms and troops to Russia. The financial windfall has fueled a rapid expansion of Pyongyang’s nuclear and naval capabilities.

The victims, primarily women and children under the age of 12, were found in mass graves showing forensic evidence of executions, including gunshot wounds and blunt force trauma.

The targeted strike on the hospital preceded another night of intense aerial bombardmen

In the Obolonskyi district, an enterprise facility was hit, with reports indicating fuel tanks had caught fire.

Ukraine's General Staff Reports 192 Clashes on Friday — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 192 combat engagements as of 10 p.m. on Friday, Aug. 7, with Russian forces launching missile strikes, guided aerial bombs (KABs) and thousands of drone attacks. The Pokrovsk direction saw the most intense fighting, with 25 assaults recorded.

Zelensky Visits Moscow-leaning Serbia for Bilateral Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Belgrade, Serbia on Friday, Aug. 7, for the first time since taking office in 2019. Zelensky said he began bilateral talks with President Aleksandar Vučić and Prime Minister Đuro Macut on economic ties, EU relations and broader security.

Russia Denies Involvement in German Airport Drone Incident — Russia's embassy in Berlin dismissed the explosive drone incident at Leipzig-Halle Airport on Friday, Aug. 7, as a staged provocation aimed at Moscow. The device was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane on Wednesday, Aug. 5, prompting a German national security review.

US Senate Passes Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill — The US Senate passed the late Lindsey O. Graham sanctions bill on Friday, Aug. 7, approving sanctions on Russia and extending Iran restrictions. The bill authorizes US President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on imports from leading buyers of Russian energy.

2 Killed, 6 Injured in Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces struck five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 50 times on Friday, Aug. 7, killing two people and injuring six others. Nikopol district continues to bear the brunt of the attacks, with private homes, apartment buildings and vehicles destroyed across several communities.

Kharkiv Authorities Hold Security Talks Ahead of Winter, After Nearly 6,000 Russian Strikes — The head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration Oleh Syniehubov and Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivsky held a joint security meeting on Friday, Aug. 7, unveiling that Russian forces have shelled the region over 5,900 times since January. Authorities said more than 16,000 residents have been evacuated this year, while preparing for the upcoming winter.

Ukraine’s BlueBird Tech Signs Defense Partnership With France’s Galion Group — Ukrainian defense technology company BlueBird Tech has signed a partnership agreement with France’s Galion Group to expand cooperation on defense innovation, attract investment, and integrate Ukrainian technologies into Europe’s defense industry through joint projects and European Defence Fund programs.

Danish Firm Unveils ‘Maritime Fortress’ to Stop Shaheds Before They Reach Odesa — Danish defense company BlueShadow expects Ukraine's Defense Ministry to certify its BlueDragon maritime air defense system by late 2026, with deployment planned for spring 2027. The company says the platform will intercept Russian Shahed drones over the Black Sea before they reach Odesa and other ports.

Military Shake-Up Poses Little Threat to Ukraine’s Drone Revolution — From AI-powered combat robots to self-charging “mechanical birds,” Ukrainian engineers are rapidly reshaping the future of warfare. Despite political upheaval in Kyiv, drone developers and frontline troops say Ukraine’s defense-tech revolution has gained too much momentum to be reversed.

US Intelligence Warns Putin Could Test NATO With Limited Attack in Coming Years — US intelligence has concluded that Vladimir Putin could test NATO with a limited military attack within the next several years, marking a major shift in Washington’s assessment as Russia faces mounting battlefield setbacks, economic strain, and growing domestic pressure.

Poland Poll: Kaczyński's PiS Slumps as Far-Right Rivals Gain — Poland's Civic Coalition (KO) remains the country's most popular political force, but its lead is narrowing as support for Law and Justice (PiS) drops sharply. A new political party backed by former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki also crossed the parliamentary threshold in the latest survey.

Not Retaliation for Wildberries – Russian Attacks Continue to Target Civilian Infrastructure Since 2022 — Despite constantly promoting the narrative that it’s “responding” to Ukrainian actions, Russia has been attacking Ukrainian facilities indiscriminately for over four years. ‘If Recruitment Fails, There Will Be Mobilization’: Russian Regions Ramp Up Cash Bonuses for War Recruiters — More than half of Russia’s regions are now paying bonuses to people who recruit contract soldiers for the war against Ukraine, with some offering up to 1 million rubles per recruit as volunteer enlistment declines and authorities increasingly rely on financial incentives to sustain military recruitment.

WATCH: Ukraine’s Sea Drones Destroy $15M Russian Air Defense — Ukraine's military intelligence said operators from its Group 13 unit destroyed a Russian Pantsir-S1 air defense system worth about $15 million and a military crane in occupied Crimea. The strike was carried out using Magura naval platforms equipped with FPV drones.

Fedorov: 200,000+ AWOL Cases Top Mobilization Crisis — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said tackling the growing number of AWOL cases should be the first goal of mobilization reform. He also argued Ukraine should overhaul its recruitment system, improve military training and allow recruits to choose their units instead of relying on punitive enforcement.

Air Defense Shortages: Can Ukraine Hold Out? — With little movement on the front lines in Ukraine, both sides are focusing their efforts on air strikes: Ukraine has decimated capacities at oil refineries in Russia with its drone attacks. Meanwhile, Moscow has launched massive missile strikes in Ukrainian cities, killing 26 people in Kyiv within one week.

Ex-US Marine Near Death in Russian Custody, Family and Advocacy Groups Say — Former US Marine Robert Gilman, imprisoned in Russia since 2022, is in critical condition and may be near death after being transferred to a psychiatric hospital, according to Reuters. US officials have urged Moscow to release him for urgent medical treatment as his family fears he may not survive.

Wildberries Hit Again: Ukrainian Drones Reach Warehouse More Than 2,000 Kilometers Inside Russia — A Ukrainian drone strike set a Wildberries warehouse ablaze in Russia’s Yekaterinburg, more than 2,000 kilometers from Ukraine’s border, as Kyiv’s long-range campaign against the retailer’s logistics network continues. More than 20 company warehouses have reportedly been hit since mid-July.

Kyiv’s Institutional Decay Deepens as EU Forces a Reckoning — Prosecutors have presented messages with senior officials allegedly trying to steer who becomes the NACP chief, while six judges from an abolished court may return to the bench. As the Verkhovna Rada delays restoring international experts to judicial selection, the EU is tying further funding to reforms Kyiv has repeatedly postponed.

Ukraine Races for Its Own Missiles as Zelensky Sets 2026–27 Domestic Breakthrough Target — Ukraine is accelerating development of its own ballistic missiles and a new anti-ballistic defense capability, with Zelensky targeting concrete results by 2026–27 as Patriot interceptor shortages leave Ukrainian cities increasingly exposed to Russian strikes.

Why Moscow’s Mayor Fears the War Economy Will ‘Kill the Country’ — Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin’s rare pushback against total economic mobilization exposes a growing dilemma over how far Russia can sacrifice its civilian economy to sustain the war.

Russian Drones Strike German-Owned Cargo Ship Off Odesa, Hit Again During Evacuation — Russian drones struck the German-owned, Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Emil off Odesa, disabling the vessel and reportedly hitting it again as its 11-member crew evacuated.
